key_insight: The number of key–value pairs a d×d linear memory can store depends critically on the retrieval rule: requiring top-1 (winner-take-all) retrieval imposes an extra logarithmic cost (d^2 ≍ n log n), and changing the retrieval criterion produces sharp capacity phase transitions.
problem_solved: Quantifies how many associations a linear (d×d) memory can reliably store and retrieve under different retrieval criteria, resolving how retrieval rules (top-1 vs listwise) change the effective storage capacity.
method: Model stored key–value pairs as isotropic Gaussian vectors and analyze retrieval success probabilistically.
Study the correlation-matrix (outer-product superposition) memory construction as the storage mechanism.
Derive sharp capacity thresholds (phase transitions) for different retrieval rules, comparing winner-take-all (top-1) and listwise criteria.
impact: Provides precise scaling laws that guide design of linear associative memories and memory-augmented models: choosing the retrieval objective can change required model size by logarithmic factors, affecting trade-offs between memory footprint and reliability.
visual_elements: Capacity plot: n (stored items) vs d^2 with threshold curves showing top-1 (d^2 ≍ n log n) and alternative retrieval regimes.
Schematic comparing retrieval rules: winner-take-all (one correct vs many distractors) vs listwise (tolerant/multi-return) with annotated failure modes.
Diagram of correlation-matrix storage: superposed outer products and how a query projects to retrieved values.
Phase diagram / heatmap illustrating sharp transitions in retrieval success probability as a function of n and d.
paper_title: Sharp Capacity Thresholds in Linear Associative Memory: From Winner-Take-All to Listwise Retrieval
paper_authors: Nicholas Barnfield, Juno Kim, Eshaan Nichani, Jason D. Lee, Yue M. Lu
